tEn: Scaling Craft at Shopify: Derek Briggs on Design as the Differentiator
tZh: 在 Shopify 规模化打磨工艺：Derek Briggs 谈设计作为差异化优势
sEn: Derek Briggs shares how he raises the craft bar at Shopify, from custom easing curves on shop.com to designing systems that scale impact across a 300-person design team.
sZh: Derek Briggs 分享他如何在 Shopify 提升工艺标准，从 shop.com 的自定义缓动曲线到通过设计系统在 300 人设计团队中放大影响力。

consensus.en: Design is the differentiator because anyone can ship an idea; craft and care set products apart.
consensus.zh: 设计是差异化因素，因为任何人都能实现想法；工艺和用心让产品脱颖而出。

consensus.en: Top-down investment from leadership gives permission to pursue quality and craft at scale.
consensus.zh: 领导层的自上而下的投入为大规模追求质量和工艺提供了许可。

consensus.en: Use longer easing durations (e.g., 400ms) while preserving a 200ms visual movement for delight.
consensus.zh: 使用更长的缓动持续时间（如400毫秒），同时保持200毫秒的视觉运动以增添愉悦感。

consensus.en: Design engineers are crucial to bridge design vision and engineering speed for high-quality interfaces.
consensus.zh: 设计工程师对于弥合设计愿景和工程速度以打造高质量界面至关重要。

consensus.en: Scale impact by documenting craft principles in markdown files and deploying them via agents.
consensus.zh: 通过将工艺原则记录在markdown文件中并通过智能体部署来扩展影响力。

consensus.en: AI should make designers 10x better, not just 10x more productive; use freed time to raise quality.
consensus.zh: AI应该让设计师好10倍，而不仅仅是多10倍的产出；利用节省的时间提升质量。

contrarian.en: Designers should spend more time on the artboard, not just prompting agents for results.
contrarian.zh: 设计师应该花更多时间在画板上，而不仅仅是提示智能体获取结果。

contrarian.en: AI struggles to innovate in design because it only presents what has happened before.
contrarian.zh: AI在设计创新上举步维艰，因为它只能呈现过去发生过的东西。

contrarian.en: Don't obsess over code quality; focus on consistency and patterns that agents can follow.
contrarian.zh: 不要过度关注代码质量；专注于智能体可以遵循的一致性和模式。

contrarian.en: Hiring many design engineers is wasteful; deploy their taste horizontally via markdown files.
contrarian.zh: 招聘大量设计工程师是浪费；通过markdown文件横向部署他们的品味。

contrarian.en: Younger designers often outperform because they lack old habits and are hungry to learn.
contrarian.zh: 年轻设计师往往表现更优，因为他们没有旧习惯且渴望学习。

contrarian.en: Less leadership is needed now because LLMs provide instant answers and enable autonomy.
contrarian.zh: 现在需要更少的领导，因为LLM提供即时答案并实现自主。

turns.en: Design is now the differentiator because anyone can come up with an idea and ship it. But it's that level of quality and care and passion that you can feel and see inside of the things that are shipped by crafters who care about all that extra little detail compared to people who are just prompting results. Welcome to Dive Club. My name is Rid and this is where designers never stop learning. This week's episode is with Derek Briggs and we're going to do a deep dive into all of the ways that he's raising the bar as a principal designer at Shopify. He screen shares how he sweats the details on the new shop.com, walks us through his custom easing curves and different ways that he's scaling impact through designing systems at Shopify. So, let's dive right in.
turns.zh: 设计如今成了差异化因素，因为任何人都能想出点子并把它发布出去。但那种品质、用心与热情，是你能从匠人交付的作品里感受到、看到的——他们在意那些额外的细小细节，而只是靠提示词出结果的人则不然。欢迎来到 Dive Club。我是 Rid，这里是设计师永不停歇的学习之地。本周的嘉宾是 Derek Briggs，我们将深入探讨他在 Shopify 担任首席设计师时提升标准的种种方式。他通过屏幕共享展示了他在新版 shop.com 上如何死磕细节，带我们了解他自定义的缓动曲线，以及他在 Shopify 通过设计系统放大影响力的不同方式。那么，让我们直接开始吧。

turns.en: Yeah, last heard from me was back at Clerk days and had an absolute blast there with that team. Obviously just a bunch of killers and I miss working with those, have continued to work with some of them and want to continue to work with them in the future. From there then head of design at Hypermode with Kevin Van Gundy. That company got acquired and I was going to take a break. But during that very short break, heard from Carl Rivera among other companies of course, but Carl and Cynthia Sevard at Shopify, she was the VP, he is the CEO, wanting me to come over to Shopify. And initially, I remember telling Cynthia like that's just not the company type that I'm built for. Like I'm more of a founding designer type. I want to work with small teams fast and iterate quickly. And she was very much like you need to talk to Carl, like that's how we're working and how we're shifting things and that's why we want you to be a part of this, because with the impact that we've seen you make at other teams, we want you to come drive that impact at a much larger scale of course, because we have a lot of teams, like the design team's like 300 some people and you know multi-thousand person engineering team to support. So intimidating for sure to get that call, but just got more and more excited about the opportunity. It being a high agency, high autonomy impact role to drive their vision, not only theirs, but the alignment that they recognized in me with their vision of a company that is super high craft, super high quality, cares more about the details than anybody else. It's been exciting.
turns.zh: 是啊，上次听到我的消息还是在 Clerk 的时候，和那支团队在一起真是无比愉快。显然那是一群狠角色，我很怀念和他们共事，也一直和其中一些人保持合作，未来还想继续合作。之后我去了 Hypermode 担任设计负责人，和 Kevin Van Gundy 一起。那家公司被收购了，我本来打算休息一阵。但就在那段很短的休息期间，我接到了 Carl Rivera 的联系——当然还有其他公司——但 Shopify 的 Carl 和 Cynthia Sevard，她是副总裁，他是 CEO，想让我加入 Shopify。起初，我记得我跟 Cynthia 说，那不是我这种类型的人适合的公司。我更像创始设计师那一类，我想和小团队快速合作、快速迭代。而她说得很明确：你得跟 Carl 聊聊，我们就是这么工作的，我们正在这样转变，这正是我们想让你加入的原因——因为看到你在其他团队产生的影响力，我们想让你在更大的规模上推动这种影响力，当然，因为我们有很多团队，设计团队大概三百多人，还有几千人的工程团队支持。接到那通电话确实让人发怵，但我对这个机会越来越兴奋。这是一个高主动性、高自主权、能产生影响力的角色，去推动他们的愿景——不只是他们的愿景，还有他们在我身上看到的、与公司愿景的一致：一家极度讲究手艺、极度追求品质、比任何人都更在意细节的公司。这一路很令人兴奋。

turns.en: The biggest change and difference in all that is, you know, in startups there's a lot of just trying things and we're trying to find product market fit. And I've learned that over my career — like earlier on I'm really trying to obsess over the details and it kind of made a name for myself throughout that. But then later on, being old and grumpy now, it's moved quick and we need to get those details in there, but we need to figure out if it's going to be worth it or not. So there's a lot of just trying very quickly. But then coming into Shopify to where there's product market fit, you know, it's a massive, extremely valuable, extremely successful company to where you're able to start thinking about we can do things that no one else can do because we can afford to invest and take the time into reaching levels of quality and innovation that other companies can't afford to do. And I've always been really excited about what does the other side of that look like for the company? And that's where I'm aimed and invested.
turns.zh: 这中间最大的变化和不同在于，你知道，在创业公司里有很多只是不断尝试，我们在努力找到产品市场契合。我在职业生涯中学到的是——早期我特别执着于细节，也因此打出了名气。但后来，现在变得又老又暴躁了，节奏要快，我们得把那些细节做进去，但也得判断它是否值得。所以有很多快速尝试。但来到 Shopify，这里已经有了产品市场契合，是一家规模巨大、极有价值、极其成功的公司，你开始可以想：我们能做别人做不到的事，因为我们负担得起投入和时间，去达到其他公司负担不起的品质与创新水平。我一直很兴奋于这家公司的另一面会是什么样，那就是我的目标和投入所在。

turns.en: I remember talking to you a couple years ago and I actually wrote a little bit of an article afterwards and there's a few points that I want to revisit in there. And the first one is you talked about the importance of top-down investment when creating this culture of craft. And you mentioned the scale and how different it is working at a company like Shopify versus something like Clerk or more of a startup environment where you can kind of just do things. I would imagine there's a little bit more of a permission angle here where some of that investment in craft and quality has to kind of come from the top. Can you talk a little bit about what that is like working at scale inside of a company like Shopify?
turns.zh: 我记得几年前和你聊过，之后我还写了一篇小文章，里面有几点我想重新聊聊。第一点是，你谈到在打造这种手艺文化时，自上而下的投入有多重要。你提到了规模，以及在 Shopify 这样的公司工作和在 Clerk 或更创业公司化的环境里工作的不同——在那里你差不多可以直接动手做。我想这里更多是一个“许可”的角度，对手艺和品质的投入必须来自高层。你能谈谈在 Shopify 这样的公司里、在规模化的情况下，那是什么感觉吗？

turns.en: Carl put out a tweet back when he was around that was an internal podcast episode called Context. There's been a few of those that have been released publicly, but it's a conversation between him and Toby around how they see design playing a role in the next era of the company and the next direction. Toby talks a lot about how design is the differentiator. Like design is now the differentiator because anyone can come up with an idea and ship it, but it's that level of quality and care and passion that you can feel and see inside of the things that are shipped by crafters who care about all that extra little detail compared to people who are just prompting results. Even though Carl's no longer at the company, it doesn't change the script for Toby. Like he still cares so much about being a leader when it comes to what we ship and the magic that comes from that. There are a lot of these memos, internal memos that he puts out a lot. He's very good at putting out almost a weekly sort of like here's a thought that I have, a letter. What I continue to tell the teams is that these things aren't necessarily telling you what to do. It's him sharing kind of his vision of where he wants things to be and giving you permission to go do it. And the people that are finding the most success are the ones that just take it and run, you know, like this is an opportunity to say something isn't good enough and just go fix it, just go be a part of that. Because no one top down is going to say, hey, hey, hey, like why are we making this better? No, no one's going to say that. We have goals, we have initiatives, we have road maps, we have things that we need to stay focused on, but there's always opportunity to make something better. The quality ambitions are very much driven by Toby and from our senior leadership.
turns.zh: Carl 还在公司的时候发过一条推文，那是一期叫 Context 的内部播客。有几期已经公开了，那是他和 Toby 之间的一场对话，谈他们如何看待设计在公司下一个时代和下一个方向中扮演的角色。Toby 经常谈到设计就是差异化因素。设计如今就是差异化因素，因为任何人都能想出点子并发布，但那种品质、用心与热情，是你能从匠人交付的作品里感受到、看到的——他们在意那些额外的细小细节，而只是靠提示词出结果的人则不然。即使 Carl 已经不在公司了，Toby 的剧本也没有变。他在我们交付什么、以及由此产生的魔力这件事上，依然非常在意做一个引领者。他经常发布很多这类备忘录，内部备忘录。他很擅长几乎每周都发一封，像是“这是我的一点想法”，一封信。我一直跟团队说的是，这些东西并不一定是在告诉你该做什么。那是他在分享他希望事情变成什么样的愿景，并给你许可去做。而那些最成功的人，就是拿到它就直接跑起来的人——这是一个机会，去说某件事还不够好，然后直接去修好它，直接参与进去。因为自上而下没有人会说：“嘿，嘿，嘿，我们为什么要把它做得更好？”不，没人会这么说。我们有目标，有倡议，有路线图，有需要保持专注的事情，但永远有机会把事情做得更好。品质上的雄心很大程度上是由 Toby 和我们的高层领导驱动的。

turns.zh: 现在，你可以在 Claude、Codex、Grok Botter 等任何你工作的地方使用 Jitter，借助全新的 Jitter MCP。我一直说 Jitter 让动画制作比任何其他工具都简单，但这真的把它提升到了另一个层次。比如，你可以在一个关于即将发布的产品会议上，会议结束后立即让 Jitter 开始探索动画社交帖子。或者你甚至可以在一个提示中让设计适应不同的宽高比。而且 MCP 创建的所有内容都是原生 Jitter 文件。所以你不只是被另一个需要从头提示的视频专家困住。你可以轻松介入并手动微调你的动画。这只是 Jitter 成为我动画首选工具的又一个原因。所以如果你想试试新的 MCP，请访问 dive.comclub/jitter。现在进入本期节目。

We have, you know, tens of thousands of merchants, extremely extremely large, successful billion-dollar company merchants and also people just getting started. Coming into that, there was a homepage adjustment happening. Design had already kind of started on what the next vision of that was going to look like or guess the next iteration. There was some big swings happening and then ultimately deciding on what's the version that we need now compared to the version that we need later because there's a lot of really incredible stuff that we have planned for Shop.com that I'm extremely excited to be a part of. I'm seeing this work happening as I'm coming in and I just think that there's still more opportunity for I just think there's more opportunity for uh just a more delightful experience. turns.zh: 最近，我进入了 Shop.com 领域。对于不熟悉 Shop.com 的人来说，shop.com 是一个汇集了 Shopify 所有商家的网站。我们有数万家商家，包括极其庞大的、成功的十亿美元级公司商家，也有刚刚起步的人。进入这个领域时，正在进行首页调整。设计已经开始了关于下一个愿景的构思，或者说是下一个迭代。有一些大的变动，然后最终决定我们现在需要的版本与以后需要的版本。因为我们对 Shop.com 有很多非常棒的计划，我非常兴奋能参与其中。我进来时看到这项工作正在进行，我只是觉得还有更多机会，我觉得还有更多机会带来更令人愉悦的体验。这是我最近才跳进去的事情。所以我带来了这个作为例子。但我们在这里看到的是轮播图，一种新的轮播图，已经在 shop.com 上线了。虽然它不错，我可以展示设计，它们略有不同。这是老生常谈的工程实现设计师设计的东西，你希望它尽可能好

turns.zh: 是的。你知道，工程师们很关心，但这需要那种额外的细节水平，我们看到并想要添加进去，你知道我们中的一些人可以做到，当然现在越来越多的人可以使用我们拥有的 AI 工具来做到。但我看到这个，这是我刚接手的第一件事，甚至不是一个倡议。它只是我看到的其他机会之一，产品路线图、人员成长、指导等等。这只是我在侧面进行的事情。但这是现在的版本。它再次不错。它传达了要点，但我只是觉得我们可以为此投入更多体验。设计本身，我和设计师合作，我们想要做，他想要做一个玻璃按钮，我正在想办法如何让这个玻璃在玻璃细节方面更好，这就是实现部分的结果。所以我一直在这里工作，即将发布的是这个版本。所以这个版本我使用 SVG 位移贴图作为背景的滤镜，在下面那个按钮上获得真正的液态玻璃感。但还有更多的事情发生了。你知道，商家的标志，我希望它是最后稳定下来的东西。就像，我们为他们展示商家。我希望它再次成为，那个商家的标志是你最后看到完成的东西，因为它是这个区域最实质的东西是那个名字。这里还有很多其他小细节。我把这个从 Swiper 重写为 Motion 的轮播引擎，这真是太棒了。你知道，Matt 非常关心 motion 包有多好，以及 ticker 组件如此高性能，性能非常重要。但我会指出这里的一些细节。所以，就像我提到的，标志本身是最后稳定下来的东西。我们这里有评分。我不会悬停它，因为悬停会暂停，但评分会微妙地动画到评分值，并与卡片本身一起动画。卡片进来的所有移动都跟踪在它自己的变量上。所以卡片上各个项目的移动基于卡片的移动。我会展示我的意思，当我拖走时，你可以看到东西反向移动。

turns.zh: 我从来不想处于这样的角色：我把事情做得更好，却没有给团队工具、理由、知识，说明为什么它变得更好。我从来不想处于这样的角色：我进来把事情做得更好，然后就离开。比如，影响文化、人们的工作方式、暴露不同的策略和技能组合，也许有人没有意识到他们有能力，这对我来说非常重要，所以当我进入一个项目，花几个月时间，让它变得更好，但我想离开时每个人都为它现在的样子感到自豪，这样如果我进入其他事情，那会继续健康。这非常非常重要。

turns.en: One of the questions that I get asked often is, "Do you want to take over a team? Do you want to lead a team? Do you want to build a team around this?" Things like that. turns.zh: 我经常被问到的一个问题是：“你想接管一个团队吗？你想领导一个团队吗？你想围绕这个建立一个团队吗？”诸如此类。我只是认为对于像 Shopify 这样的公司来说，现在这不是最健康的事情。因为 Shopify 越来越自主地成为公司伟大的领域，只是弄清楚需要做什么才能成为迄今为止最好的版本。对我来说，围绕这个影响建立一个团队。当然，我们可以跳来跳去这样做，但我真的想与人们一起工作，我真的想通过向他们展示什么是可能的，而不是谈论什么是可能的，来影响他们的个人贡献。这从来都不是真正让我兴奋的事情。

turns.en: And I think from a leadership perspective that there's just less and less leadership needed these days being that with all of our LLMs and AI tooling that we have, there are so many answers to get instantly. turns.zh: 我认为从领导力的角度来看，如今需要的领导力越来越少，因为我们拥有所有的 LLM 和 AI 工具，可以立即获得很多答案。你有任何问题，都可以让它发生。我当然抓住了这一点。我运行了很多基于客户如何使用某物的产品机会的自动化，向我展示关于这个没有像你想象的那样转化的想法。所以，这里有一些关于我们如何重新处理这个的想法。就像很多这些循环运行，不断挤出它可能更好的地方。我就是如此痴迷于事情总是不够好。我认为这是我的优点也是我的缺点。

turns.zh: 这是一个有趣的时期，感觉团队中一些最有影响力的人能够扩展自己和他们带来的东西。我有一个问题，也许我们可以用它作为招聘的过渡。我认为这是你想引入团队的一种人。也许更多是产品设计师，也许更多是关于工艺。我不太确定。但是当你想到你想引入 Shopify 的梦想人选，继续提高工艺和质量的标准时，你具体在寻找哪些东西？比如我们能不能谈谈你对新员工的评估流程，因为我知道你现在正在招聘多个不同的职位。

turns.en: Yeah, it's really important to me that folks are not using AI to do 10 times more work. It's important to me that it's making them 10 times better. So, what they used to be doing by hand all of the time and they're extremely good at, how can they make that even better? Like, how can they make the quality of that output even better? I also can sense some folks just getting lazier like that. And again, that's that's the part of the doing 10 times more work because like they're they're like, "All right, I can automate all of this stuff. I what I could do now, I can do a bunch of."
turns.zh: 是的，对我来说非常重要的是，人们不是用 AI 来做 10 倍的工作量。对我来说重要的是，它让他们变得 10 倍更好。所以，他们过去一直手工做的、非常擅长的事情，他们如何能做得更好？比如，他们如何能让输出的质量更好？我也能感觉到有些人变得懒惰了。再说一次，这就是做 10 倍工作量的部分，因为他们就像，“好吧，我可以自动化所有这些。我现在能做的，我可以做一堆。”

turns.en: Yeah, that's so true.
turns.zh: 是的，太对了。

turns.en: And we all do that, but what are you doing with the extra time? And that's I think the thing that's really important to me is that I'm spending the extra time that's now freed up and how can I make my work even better and right now is influencing other people and influencing the output of other folks on our teams to reach their capability that maybe they didn't feel like they were that that was possible. So, it's a lot of sort of thought sharing and and what I'm doing to inspire them so that they can start doing more of this stuff too. And again, that compounds across, you know, additional quality and speed throughout the company.
turns.zh: 我们都会这样做，但你把额外的时间用来做什么？我认为对我来说真正重要的是，我把现在腾出来的额外时间用来如何让我的工作更好，而现在就是影响其他人，影响我们团队中其他人的输出，让他们达到他们可能觉得不可能达到的能力。所以，这很多是思想分享，以及我在做什么来激励他们，让他们也开始做更多这样的事情。再说一次，这会在整个公司中复合，带来额外的质量和速度。

turns.en: But yeah, so I'm looking for people that are just hungry, and they've embraced that we are capable of things that we've never thought we were capable of — not only through skill sets that you didn't have before, like technical skill sets that now you can build. But now you can build doesn't feel good enough. It's what you realize you're capable of building that's most important. It's that hunger of "I couldn't do this thing before, so how far can I take it?"
turns.zh: 不过说到底，我在找的是那种特别有渴望的人，他们已经接受了这一点：我们能做成以前从没想过自己能做成的事——不只是靠你以前没有的技能，比如现在你能掌握的技术技能。但“现在你能做”还不够，真正重要的是你意识到自己有能力做出什么。就是那种渴望：“我以前做不了这件事，那我能把它推到多远？”

turns.en: And I'm really excited about the people. Funny enough, it tends to be the younger crowd, the newer-to-the-industry crowd — they're not caught in these old ways and they don't understand how it was before. So they're just so much better automatically at what they're doing because they don't have any old habits to break. And they're hungry. They have so much more time to spend on this.
turns.zh: 我对这些人特别兴奋。有意思的是，往往是比较年轻的一群人、刚入行的一群人——他们没有被那些老路子困住，也不了解以前是什么样。所以他们做起事来天然就强得多，因为没有旧习惯要打破。而且他们有渴望，有更多时间投入这件事。

turns.en: And gosh, I couldn't imagine where I would be 15 years ago, when I was just sitting on the couch on HTML Dog figuring out how to write HTML and CSS because I was frustrated that the engineers weren't building the things that looked the same as my Photoshop files. But what a time to be alive. It's just crazy.
turns.zh: 天哪，我都不敢想象 15 年前的我会是什么样——那时我就坐在沙发上逛 HTML Dog，琢磨怎么写 HTML 和 CSS，因为我很沮丧：工程师做出来的东西跟我 Photoshop 文件里的样子不一样。但能活在这个时代真好，简直不可思议。
